subject: Post-call: Performance guardrails & VPC validation for FinApps private deploy
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Meyer <alex.meyer@finapps.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Performance guardrails & VPC validation for FinApps private deploy

Alex — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on during the call so we can move the private/VPC perf validation forward. Please see the checklist and the immediate requests below.

Call highlights (short):
- FinApps target: conversational streaming use case (agent + generative summaries) with p99 tail target of 80ms for token streaming inside the VPC, and 200ms end-to-end from client to Redwood-hosted model for routed fallback.
- Expected sustained concurrency: 120 concurrent streaming sessions during peak (each ~6 tokens/sec average), burst to 300 for 15–30s windows.
- Throughput: expect up to ~45 tokens/sec aggregated per GPU during bursts; planning for an initial pool of 4 GPUs (we'll run capacity sims).
- Acceptable fallback behavior: when private pool saturated, route to dedicated-hosted with model variant M-medium (quantized) with transparent fallback and <500ms cold-start fallback SLA.

Immediate asks (what we need from FinApps SRE):
1) Network traces (pcap) or tcpdump from the path between FinApps app servers and the VPC peering endpoint for a 30m window during peak — ideally the same timeframe you captured yesterday. Attach as .pcap.
2) Confirmation of egress bandwidth available (Gbps) and the typical MTU; any packet shaping/firewall appliances in the path.
3) List of IP ranges and subnets that will be used for the peering + any NAT/masquerade hops.
4) TLS termination point for gRPC/HTTP streaming and whether there is an L7 proxy that will buffer streaming chunks.
5) SRE contact + preferred window for a short validation run (30–60 min) next week (we can run synthetic streaming load and a real token-level tracing session).

Attachments we will produce from our side after we ingest your pcap: a latency hop breakdown, KV-cache hit maps, and a MAP_SLO_TABLE_v1.xlsx (initial acceptance thresholds).

Next steps (owner):
- Alex: share pcap, bandwidth, and IP ranges (today if possible).
- Ben: will scope the synthetic validation and share the test script and expected load profile by EOD today.
- Marissa: coordinate internal compliance check for data-in-transit logs and capture retention window (we will flag what we store).

Thanks — aim is to have a short validation next Tue/Wed and produce an acceptance note for your networking team.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

---

Cc: FinApps SRE <sre@finapps.io>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance guardrails & VPC validation for FinApps private deploy

Thanks Karthik — good summary. Per our notes: attaching the 25m tcpdump from yesterday's peak window (VPN->peering hop). We ran this during the 11:30–11:55 window when spike occurred.

Quick answers inline:
1) pcap attached: network_trace_20270927.pcap (see attachment). We captured SYN/ACK patterns and some intermittent retransmits around 11:40 — looks like a micro-burst on one of our firewall appliances.
2) Egress: our peered link is 10Gbps but currently provisioned with 7Gbps average available (we're on a shared infra lane). We can provision a temporary increase to 9Gbps for the validation window if needed. MTU is 1500; there is a corporate IDS that does TLS inspection in front of the peering edge (it does not terminate TLS, but does mirror flows).
3) IP ranges: 10.12.0.0/18 (app subnets), NAT egress via 34.198.120.0/28 (static).
4) TLS termination: app -> L7 proxy (Envoy) terminates TLS for internal routing; outbound gRPC to the peering endpoint uses mutual TLS from Envoy (we can provide cert/thumbprint). Envoy is configured for streaming passthrough — it should not buffer beyond 16KB chunks, but we will confirm.
5) SRE contact: cc:daniel.ho@sre.finapps.io. Available windows: Wed 2027-09-29 10:00–12:00 PT or Thu 2027-09-30 14:00–16:00 PT. Please pick one.

Observations from the pcap (quick):
- The retransmit cluster aligns with a firewall CPU spike — we are investigating a perf tuning for that appliance.
- No obvious long RTT; one-way latency (approx) from capture is ~18–22ms to the peering edge. That leaves ~30–60ms budget for internal hops and Redwood-side processing to hit your 80ms p99 token target for in-VPC streaming.

We'll provision the temporary egress bump if the Redwood test requires it. Let us know the exact IP:port for the validation endpoint and any specific TLS root certs.

Alex Meyer
Head of Platform Engineering
FinApps

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Meyer <alex.meyer@finapps.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance guardrails & VPC validation for FinApps private deploy

Appreciate the pcap and the quick turn, Alex. A few follow-ups from our infra perf side so we can shape the synthetic run and acceptance table (I've attached the initial MAP_SLO_TABLE_v1.xlsx and will update after we validate your pcap).

Technical asks / clarifications:
- Can you confirm whether Envoy is doing any per-connection rate-limiting or global connection limits? If so, what are the limits (connections/sec, concurrent streams)?
- Please confirm NAT timeouts for the egress IPs (we've seen sessions dropped when NAT timeouts <60s during low token bursts).
- Do you have any L4 load balancer in front of Envoy that performs health checks which may induce short-lived connection churn?
- For the temporary validation we will open 4 worker grequests from the test harness (simulating 120 concurrent streams total by multiplexing) and run three 10-minute ramps: 1) baseline steady 120 sessions, 2) burst to 300 sessions, 3) cooldown. We'll capture token-level latencies at 1ms granularity and KV-cache heatmaps. Does that plan work?

Acceptance criteria (draft — see MAP_SLO_TABLE_v1.xlsx):
- In-VPC streaming p99 token latency <= 80ms (target), p95 <= 40ms
- End-to-end client->fallback < 500ms when routed to hosted fallback (cold model start allowed once per 30m window)
- No more than 1% packet retransmit rate sustained over a 5m window for the peering path during test
- Sustained throughput supporting 45 tokens/sec/GPU during burst windows with <5% token drop on network backpressure

If you confirm Envoy limits and NAT timeouts we can finalize the test script and run Wed 10:00 PT. We will also provide a short pre-test checklist (IP allowlist entry, cert thumbprint, and an ephemeral validation endpoint).

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP_SLO_TABLE_v1.xlsx

Thanks Ben — that's helpful. Quick answers:
- Envoy: no global connection limit configured today; per-listener limits are default. We do have a per-route rate limit for some legacy endpoints (not the streaming route) — confirmed: streaming route has no rate-limit.
- NAT timeouts: default NAT idle timeout is 120s.
- L4 balancer: yes, we have a fronting GCP/LB performing health checks every 10s; it should not cause churn but worth noting.
- Wed 2027-09-29 10:00–12:00 PT won't work for us (we have a security ops maintenance window). Thu 2027-09-30 14:00–16:00 PT works. Please run the validation then.

We will:
- Provision a temporary egress bump to 9Gbps for Thu 14:00–16:00 PT.
- Place a temporary allowlist for Redwood test IPs (please provide those IPs).
- Provide the Envoy cert thumbprint via a secure channel (I will share with your infra contact).

If you can confirm the exact test IPs and a short pre-test checklist by EOD Wed, we'll lock the Thu window. Otherwise, we can move to the following week.

Alex
Head of Platform Engineering
FinApps
